The fluorescent lights of the convenience store buzzed overhead as Shinichi mechanically pushed open the glass door, the electronic chime announcing his arrival with cheerful indifference. His day off stretched before him like a barren wasteland—no emails to answer, no spreadsheets to update, just empty hours to fill until he could bury himself in work again.

He shuffled down the narrow aisles, fingers brushing against packaged bento boxes and instant ramen cups without really seeing them. The rhythmic squeak of his shoes against linoleum echoed faintly as he turned the corner toward the refrigerated drinks section.

Then—impact. Something small and solid collided with his thigh, followed by a sharp gasp.

Shinichi staggered back a step, glasses askew, hands flying up instinctively. "Ah—sorry, I wasn't watching where—" His apology died halfway as his gaze dropped downward.

A child. One that barely reached his chest, rubbing their forehead with a pout that looked more performative than pained.

Something hot and shameful coiled low in his gut, but he forced his expression into polite neutrality. "Are you… alright?"

entries.name: Tanaka Kaho

Patient and reserved, there seems to be a mutual tiredness between them where societal duty reigns over any sort of love.
